The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2,3}=2\pm 3\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =1(x-3)(x-(2+3\text{i}))(x-(2-3\text{i})) \\  & =(x-3)(x-(2+3\text{i}))(x-(2-3\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)(x-(2+3\text{i}))(x-(2-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-3)({x}^{2}-x(2-3\text{i})-x(2+3\text{i})+(2+3\text{i})(2-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-3)({x}^{2}-4x+13) & = \\ {x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+13x-3{x}^{2}+12x-39 & = \\ {x}^{3}-7{x}^{2}+25x-39 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{3}-7{x}^{2}+25x-39.$
